comment: Budgets and baselines for scripts/benchmark-latency.mjs. A budget is the product
limit for one stage of 'a new session is visible in the desktop in < 5 ms' (p99,
release build); `enforced: false` marks a stage the code does not meet yet, whose
breach is reported but does not fail the gate. The change that brings a stage under
its budget flips it to `enforced: true` in the same pull request. Baselines are
per platform class and are recorded on that class with --update-baselines; see

regressionComment: Enforced stages (within budget on that class): p99 at/over budget fails; p99 more than maxRegression
over the base commit, measured interleaved on the same runner (--base), fails. Stored baselines decide
only with no base and on a CPU in cpusSeen; the same metric was 20-40% apart on two runners of one class.
Tracked stages (known over budget, current numbers in each budget's `known`): over budget is an expected
failure; getting worse fails, judged on p50 because their tails are lock waits that land on random
samples. Worse = p50 more than trackedMaxRegression over the base AND more than maxRegression over the
known p50: on identical code these stages moved 12-27% between interleaved base and head runs, so
either test alone fails healthy pull requests.
Every bound adds max(regressionFloorMs, regressionFloorBudgetShare x the stage's budget): a no-change
A/B on a busy machine moved the raw fs-event p99 0.15 -> 0.60 ms over 100 samples.

stages@30d.fs_event.enforcedComment: FSEvents on the macos-latest runner (Apple M1, virtual) delivered at 15.7 ms p50 / 19 ms p99 with notify's latency 0.0 and NoDefer; inotify meets the budget at 0.13 ms. Enforced where it is met.

stages@30d.sweep_scoped_sync.stage: parse + SQLite txn (watch tick / collector sweep)

stages@30d.list_first_paint.enforcedComment: macos-latest is a 3-vCPU Apple M1 VM: p50 0.20-0.28 ms, but its p99 tail went 0.53 -> 1.72 ms between two runs on the same CPU model. Tracked there until a real M-series runner measures it.

list_scale@30d.list_desktop_page.enforcedComment: Its own budget, not the 1.5 ms first paint: the desktop's 500-row page (SESSION_LIST_LIMIT) is filled after the first 50 rows are on screen, so it is not on the 5 ms new-session path. 4.0 ms p99 is ~1.5x the ubuntu-latest p99 (2.45 ms at 30 days, 2.60 ms at a year) and ~1.3x the macOS VM's (2.9-3.0 ms), so it fails a real regression in the catalog query or row decoding without failing the page size itself. Enforced on linux-x64; tracked on the macOS VM, whose worst round reached 3.97 ms. Proposed by W0, pending Khaliq's confirmation of the number.

ingest_upload@30d.ingest_with_uploader.stage: parse + SQLite txn while an uploader runs

prune@365d.read_during_prune.enforcedComment: macos-latest read 1.47-1.79 ms p99 during a 1-year prune (0.54-0.70 ms quiet); linux-x64 0.52-0.75 ms. Enforced where it is met.

prune@365d.ingest_during_prune.stage: parse + SQLite txn while retention prunes

gate.description: The pull-request gate: release build, 40 sessions a day, a 30-day and a 1-year store, three rounds per run.

full.description: The published matrix: the gate's runs with more samples and rounds.

smoke.description: Seconds-long check that the driver, the base worktree and every phase run; its numbers mean nothing.
